hints: Focus on the Group 2 trend for reaction with water, reactivity increases as you go down the group from magnesium to barium.
Notice that $\text{BaO}$ forms $\text{Ba(OH)}_2$ which is far more soluble than the $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$ formed from $\text{MgO}$.
Connect solubility to pH, the test-tube with less dissolved $\text{OH}^-$ will be less alkaline and so have the lower pH.
walkthrough:
**Recall the Group 2 oxide trend**

Think of Group 2 going down: Mg at the top, Ba near the bottom. Reactivity with water and solubility of hydroxides both increase down the group.

So $\text{BaO}$ reacts more readily and more vigorously than $\text{MgO}$.

**Write what happens in water**

Both oxides form a metal hydroxide, which is alkaline:
$$\text{MgO} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Mg(OH)}_2$$
$$\text{BaO} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Ba(OH)}_2$$

**Link solubility to pH of the filtrate**

We use excess solid, so each filtrate is a saturated solution. $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$ is only sparingly soluble, so test-tube X contains very little $\text{OH}^-$.

$\text{Ba(OH)}_2$ is much more soluble, so test-tube Y contains a lot more $\text{OH}^-$ and has a higher pH. Therefore the filtrate of lower pH is X.

options.A: Correct. Barium oxide is lower in Group 2 so reacts more readily with water. Its hydroxide is more soluble, giving more OH- and higher pH in Y, so X (magnesium filtrate) has the lower pH.
options.B: Half right but pH is reversed. Students often think the more reactive oxide gives the lower pH. In fact more reaction and greater solubility means more OH- and a higher pH, so Y cannot be lower than X.
options.C: Incorrect reactivity order. Magnesium oxide is at the top of Group 2 and reacts only slightly with water to give a weakly alkaline suspension, while barium oxide reacts much more readily.
options.D: Both parts are wrong. It reverses the Group 2 trend. Reactivity and hydroxide solubility increase down the group, so BaO is more reactive and MgO filtrate (X) is less alkaline.
